title: Minimize GPU startup jitter and unify kernel discovery flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We frequently observe non-deterministic cold-start latency spikes (startup jitter) in mixed-GPU pools. Root causes include ad-hoc kernel probing order, N+1 probing of CUTLASS/Triton variants, on-demand shared-object loads, and duplicate work from multiple processes warming the same kernels concurrently. This ticket centralizes the discovery and early-warmup flow to reduce P95/P99 init time and decrease failed-kernel fallbacks during scale events.

Goals: 1) Replace parallel per-process probe heuristics with a single coordinated discovery step per node and a lightweight probe cache. 2) Introduce a deterministic kernel ordering and preference table mapping model variant -> preferred kernel bundle to avoid unnecessary fallbacks. 3) Add an opt-in early-warmup phase during node admission to pre-load hot quant and attention kernels. 4) Expose metrics and alarms for probe failures and init time regressions; provide a console dashboard for rollout.

Approach: - Implement a node-level probe coordinator (PID-based lock + file-backed probe cache) that records GPU capability, available kernel bundles, and preferred load order. - Build a small deterministic kernel preference manifest (generated at build or via model onboarding job) that the runtime consults instead of heuristics. - Add a configurable early-warmup worker that sequentially loads top-N kernels using a rate-limited loader to avoid I/O storms. - Make the coordinator backward-compatible: fall back to current probing path if coordinator unavailable and surface detailed logs for debugging. - Feature-flag the new flow and gate warmup on capacity tier and canary labels.

Why unique: Rather than only pruning or sequencing probes, this consolidates discovery state to avoid duplicate probing, reduces heat from concurrent loads, and creates a build-time manifest to cut heuristic divergence between environments.
acceptance_criteria: Node-level probe coordinator implemented and enabled behind feature flag
Probe cache persists across short-lived worker restarts and lowers total probe attempts by >=40% in lab runs
P95 cold-start init time reduces by >=30% in controlled canary (same model mix)
Fallback kernel load rate decreases and failed_kernel_loads metric shows a drop of >=50%
No customer-facing errors introduced in canary; safe rollback via feature flag
Documentation for manifest generation and ops runbook completed
rollout_plan: 1) Implement coordinator + manifest generation in feature branch. 2) Run node-level simulation and lab validation against mixed workload harness. 3) Canary rollout to 2% of Dedicated pools (low-impact region) for 48 hours; monitor init_time_p50/p95/p99, failed_kernel_loads, oom/eviction rates. 4) Expand canary to 20% and run workload for 7 days. 5) Full roll when metrics stable and ops sign-off. Always keep feature flag and quick rollback path.
risks: Coordinator bug could cause missed kernel discovery and increased cold failures
Early warmup could cause transient memory pressure on small GPUs if limits misconfigured
Manifest drift between build-time and deployed kernel bundles could cause mismatches
Race conditions when multiple node agents try to write to shared probe cache under heavy churn
test_plan: Unit tests for probe coordinator state machine, integration tests for manifest lookup and fallback path, e2e lab runs with synthetic workloads (short/long sequences) to measure init latencies. Add stress test that simulates simultaneous node joins to validate rate-limiting. Include GPU memory budget checks during warmup. Add canary asserts to block expansion if P95 increases >10%.
